findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is removed from the wrong store
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now prefers the credential returned by the user storage's `getCredentials()`. When that federated credential reports `allCodesUsed()`, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only operates on the local Keycloak DB. The ID belongs to the user-storage credential, so the call is a no-op (or, if the storage did not set an ID, passes `null` into the JPA store). The exhausted credential stays in the user storage, `isConfiguredFor(recovery-authn-codes)` remains true, and the user will keep being challenged for a recovery code they cannot satisfy until the required action completes. For federated credentials the removal should go through the storage (e.g. `disableCredentialType`) rather than the local store.

findings.title: Login form throws NoSuchElementException when storage accepts recovery codes but does not expose them via getCredentials()
findings.body: With this PR a user storage provider that returns true from `supportsCredentialType`/`updateCredential`/`isConfiguredFor` for `recovery-authn-codes` will own the credential, and the authenticator's `configuredFor()` will return true. However `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` has a default empty implementation, so `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns an empty Optional for any provider that implements validation but not `getCredentials()`. `credentialModelOpt.get()` (and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on line 21) then throw `NoSuchElementException` while rendering the recovery-code login page, producing a 500 for every such user. The new implicit requirement that providers implement `getCredentials()` is neither enforced nor documented; the bean should handle the absent case gracefully (e.g. omit the code number) instead of failing the login.

findings.title: Undocumented wire contract: raw recovery codes passed to user storage as an ad-hoc JSON array
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` sends the plaintext recovery codes to `CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential` as a JSON-serialized `List<String>` in the `challengeResponse` of a `UserCredentialModel` with an empty id. Nothing in the SPI (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, `UserCredentialModel`, javadoc, constants) describes this format, so third-party storage providers have no way to know what they receive, that the codes are unhashed, or that they are responsible for hashing them and for marking codes as consumed in `isValid`. A provider that does not hash will persist recovery codes in clear text. The format should be documented on the SPI (ideally with a typed model/constant, similar to how OTP uses the OTP policy type) and the javadoc should state the provider's hashing/consumption responsibilities.

findings.title: Backwards-compatibility provider now depends on APIs that post-date 4.8.3 and can NPE
findings.body: This class's javadoc states it is a frozen 4.8.3-era provider whose purpose is to prove newer Keycloak still works with old provider code. The PR adds an `@Override` of `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` and uses `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, neither of which existed in 4.8.3, so the provider no longer tests what the javadoc claims. Additionally `getCredentials` dereferences `getMyUser(user)` without the null check that every other method in this class performs, so a user removed from the map (or a user with a mismatched username case) will throw NPE from `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`.

findings.title: Test storage never consumes recovery codes, so the new test cannot detect consumption/exhaustion regressions
findings.body: `isValid` for recovery codes does a plaintext `anyMatch` and never marks a code as used, and `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` from the raw list on every call, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` is always code 0 and `allCodesUsed()` is never true. Consequently `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` asserting `expectedCode == 0` is trivially satisfied and nothing exercises reuse rejection, second-code login, exhaustion → required action, or disabling (`disableCredentialType` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` also ignore recovery codes, so admin/account removal of federated recovery codes is untested and would silently leave them in place).
